children: said Wednesday it ​was selected by the Trump administration as a founding partner in the launch of VaultCo, a strategic critical minerals reserve designed to strengthen U.S. critical minerals supply chains, through a $500M commitment from the Export-Import Bank of the United States.

The company said the VaultCo public-private partnership will ⁠enable it to source, procure, and deliver critical minerals ​to ​the ⁠U.S. and reduce any future ​disruptions to ​the ⁠country's supply of critical minerals.

The Trump administration is developing a ~$12B stockpile of critical minerals that would be comparable to the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, a store of crude oil first established during the 1970s energy crisis.
Separately, U.S. metals refining startup Nth Cycle ​said it signed a $1B offtake agreement with Glencore
to supply lithium and other critical minerals extracted from ‌recycled batteries, a deal that comes ahead of a planned IPO later this year.
As part of the deal, Glencore
will sell Nth ​Cycle ~24K metric tons/year of shredded battery parts known as black mass for it to process, essentially supplying ​the feedstock from which to extract the minerals.

title: Glencore to partner with U.S. EXIM Bank to build strategic minerals reserve fund
